summary: This script launches lazydocker (a Docker management UI) in a container, mounting your current working directory so it can see and manage any docker-compose files you have locally. It uses exec to replace the shell process with the Docker command, so when you exit lazydocker, you exit the script cleanly.

explanations.7: set -euo pipefail makes the script strict: it exits immediately if any command fails (-e), treats undefined variables as errors (-u), and fails if any command in a pipeline fails (-o pipefail).
explanations.9: exec replaces the current shell process with the docker run command, so there's no lingering shell after lazydocker exits.
explanations.10: This mounts the Docker daemon socket into the container so lazydocker inside the container can communicate with Docker on your host machine.
explanations.11: This creates a named volume to persist lazydocker's configuration between runs, so your settings don't get lost when the container stops.
explanations.12: This mounts your current directory (PWD = present working directory) into the container at /workdir so lazydocker can find your compose.yaml file.
explanations.13: This tells the container to start with /workdir as its working directory, so lazydocker looks there first for docker-compose files.
